content.title: Netanyahu death rumours debunked amid war
content.text: AI imagery and optical illusion fuelled speculation The death rumours began after a March 12 video of Netanyahu was claimed to be AI-generated due to an apparent ‘six fingers’ anomaly. Fact-checkers including Grok and PolitiFact confirmed he has five fingers on each hand, attributing the illusion to camera angles, lighting, and gesture. Similar AI-generated fake images showing him injured in rubble were also flagged and debunked by credible outlets such as Snopes and The Jerusalem Post. Hindustan Times + 4 Social media silence of Yair Netanyahu added intrigue Attention shifted to Netanyahu’s son Yair, usually a prolific poster on X, who had not posted new content since March 8, though he reposted on March 9. This five-day gap led some users to speculate about a family tragedy, despite no official confirmation. Analysts note such personal behaviour shifts can influence public perception, especially during crises. Hindustan Times + 3 Official denials counter Iranian and online claims Netanyahu’s office dismissed Iranian media claims of attacks on him or his family as fake news. Grok fact-checks, along with Snopes and Times of Israel, confirmed there were no credible reports of his death or injury. Officials emphasised that Netanyahu remains in Israel, actively leading military and diplomatic efforts against Iran. Newspoint + 4 Conflict backdrop linked to surge in claims Speculation over Netanyahu’s safety coincided with the Israel–Iran conflict, during which joint US–Israel strikes killed former Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Khamenei. The March 12 press conference, his first since the latest war began, included announcements about killing several top Iranian nuclear scientists and was followed by the posting of the speech online. These high-profile wartime developments were accompanied by a rise in unverified social media narratives about his wellbeing. Hindustan Times + 3 12 references More for you
